No historical research or external model-service call is used. In it, two disjoint-from-c lines can meet; parallel verticals cut by a semicircle have corresponding angles 90 and 120 degrees; and the triangle (0,1),(1,1),(0,2) has angle sum 163.739795 degrees. option_checks.evidence: A proves the theorem because an intersection of distinct a,b parallel to c would produce two parallels through one point. Conversely, the transitivity assertion implies A: two different parallels to l through X would have to be parallel to each other yet share X. Thus it is equivalent to A. Explicit neutral failure: in the upper half-plane, c:x=0, b:x=1 and a:(x-1)^2+y^2=1/4, y>0, are pairwise distinct. Both a and b are disjoint from c, but they intersect at (1,1/2).
For AB=AC, compare ABC with ACB by neutral SSS: AB=AC, AC=AB and BC=CB. Congruence exchanges vertices B,C, giving equal base angles. Neither parallel construction nor A is used.

The FORWARD parallel-angle theorem is not neutral. In the upper half-plane, parallel lines x=0,x=1 cut by x^2+y^2=4, y>0, meet at (0,2),(1,sqrt(3)). For upward vertical rays and the same clockwise/eastward transversal direction, tangents (1,0),(sqrt(3),-1) give corresponding angles 90 and 120 degrees. Also the universal forward theorem implies A: take a perpendicular transversal from X to l; every parallel through X must form a right corresponding angle, hence equal the unique perpendicular there. This does not refute the neutral converse in 444, whose equal-angle premise is absent in the example.

The Euclidean vertex-parallel proof of triangle sum uses A through forward parallel-angle equalities. Intrinsic neutral failure is explicit: in the upper-half-plane triangle U=(0,1), V=(1,1), W=(0,2), UW is vertical, UV is centered at (1/2,0), and VW at (-1,0). The tangent angles are arctan(2), arctan(3/4), arctan(2). Their sum is 2*arctan(2)+arctan(3/4)=163.739795291688 degrees, not 180. Hence neutral properties alone cannot give the universal equality.

The triangle inequality is neutral. Extend BA beyond A to D with AD=AC, so BD=BA+AC. Isosceles ACD gives angle ADC=angle ACD, and collinearity gives angle BDC=angle ADC. Since CA is interior to BCD, angle BCD>angle ACD=angle BDC. Neutral opposite-side/angle comparison yields BD>BC, hence BA+AC>BC. That comparison follows from marking the shorter side on the longer, isosceles base angles and the strict neutral exterior-angle theorem, with the converse by length trichotomy. Relabeling yields every two-side inequality, with no A or triangle-angle sum.
